papers.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
papers.abstract: Agentic workloads are a major source of LLM inference demand. Existing prefill--decode (PD) disaggregated serving systems offer limited flexibility for runtime adaptation of compute allocation and KV cache management, and rely on coarse signals that only partly capture the diverse and dynamic agent workload. These limitations lead to load imbalance between prefill and decode nodes and eviction of KV caches that agents will reuse. papers.title: PACE: Keeping the Right Tokens in the KV Cache Is Not Enough for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents accumulate sessions of up to millions of tokens, far more key-value (KV) cache than one GPU holds, so serving systems keep a small budget of tokens and evict the rest. papers.title: Energy-Harvesting-Aware Cell-Free LEO Satellite Networks: A Lyapunov Framework for Sustainable User-Centric Beamforming and Clustering
papers.abstract: We study battery-aware downlink control in user-centric cell-free low Earth orbit satellite networks with intermittent solar harvesting and finite onboard batteries. A perturbed Lyapunov controller coordinates clustering and hybrid beamforming using measured battery states and causal harvest forecasts. The per-slot solver combines group-sparse association, rate bounds, a quadratic transform, and successive convex approximation. We establish robust battery invariance for feasible implemented actions and give a utility bound conditional on a comparison policy and the per-slot implementation gap.
